title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-11-19
lineage: Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC (1 Disc Audio / 1 Disc FLAC)

ai_review.summary: A pristine soundboard capture of the legendary 11/19/66 show, highlighted by Pigpen‑driven classics like Cream Puff War and Hi‑Heel Sneakers.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised for its crystal‑clear stereo mix and faithful transfer work by Charlie Miller, delivering an almost modern listening experience of a 1966 performance. Musically the show shines with an early‑Dead vibe—Pigpen dominates the setlist, delivering powerhouse versions of Cream Puff War, Hi‑Heel Sneakers, Same Thing and a rare Otis Redding cover—though one listener notes a sudden cut‑out during the middle of “Dancin’ in the Street.” Overall the performance is celebrated as one of the finest snapshots of the band’s formative era.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, extolling both the music and the superb soundboard transfer; only minor technical complaints lower the rating slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo Hi‑Fi mix praised as crisp, clear and well‑balanced; occasional issues mentioned include a mid‑song cut‑out in “Dancin’ in the Street,” channel/pitch quirks that some users corrected, but overall the transfer is considered top‑tier.

standout_songs: Pain In My Heart (Otis Redding cover)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑Dead set with a strong Pigpen‑fronted first half, followed by an all‑Pigpen second set; the energy stays high throughout despite one reported abrupt ending of a jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Briefly joins on “Teddy Bear's Picnic” (mentioned in technical notes).
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ described as bubbly, powerful and central to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Confusion over Bill Kreutzmann’s alias ‘Bill Summers’ clarified; drummer recognized for solid early‑Dead rhythms.
